Theme

# Philosophy quotes about experience

Experience is the lived encounter with world and self—foundation or limit for knowledge, art, and ethics.

23 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Empiricists treat experience as the source of ideas; phenomenologists describe its structure; pragmatists treat it as experimental and revisable.

## In the history of philosophy

From Aristotelian aisthesis to Locke, Hume, Dewey, and phenomenology, experience is a battleground for epistemology and metaphysics.

## Thinkers in this collection

[John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke) , [George Berkeley](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/george-berkeley) , [David Hume](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/david-hume) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [John Dewey](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-dewey) , [Alfred North Whitehead](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/alfred-north-whitehead) , [Nishida Kitaro](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/nishida-kitaro) , [Al-Ghazali](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/al-ghazali)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is experience in philosophy?

It is the first-person undergoing of sensations, thoughts, and situations—interpreted differently across schools.

### Is all knowledge from experience?

Empiricists lean yes; rationalists and others defend a priori elements or innate structures.
